hints.concept: Think about what the last valid index of an array should be.
hints.guidance: An array with length n usually has valid indexes from 0 up to n - 1.
hints.targeted: Check whether this loop condition should stop before the array length instead of including the length value.

hints.concept: A condition should normally check a value rather than change it.
hints.guidance: Look at the operator inside this condition and decide whether it is comparing two values.
hints.targeted: Check whether the condition uses assignment where a comparison was intended.

hints.concept: Array length tells you how many items exist, not the last valid position.
hints.guidance: Compare the number of elements with the final usable index.
hints.targeted: Check whether the array length is being used directly as an index.

hints.concept: Strings are objects, so == asks whether two variables point to the same object, not whether the text matches.
hints.guidance: Think about the difference between comparing object references and comparing the characters inside two strings.
hints.targeted: Check whether this comparison should use the .equals() method instead of == or !=.

hints.concept: A loop only finishes when its counter eventually makes the condition false.
hints.guidance: Follow the counter value for a few iterations and see whether it moves toward or away from the loop bound.
hints.targeted: Check whether the update step moves the counter in the direction the condition expects.

hints.concept: A return statement immediately ends the method; nothing after it in the same block can run.
hints.guidance: Trace the method line by line and note the exact point where execution leaves the method.
hints.targeted: Check whether the statements after this return were meant to run before it.

hints.concept: In a switch, execution continues into the next case unless something like break stops it.
hints.guidance: Walk through what happens after this case's statements finish and which case runs next.
hints.targeted: Check whether this case should end with a break before the next case begins.

hints.concept: A semicolon on its own is a complete, empty statement.
hints.guidance: Look closely at what the condition actually controls when a semicolon comes right after the closing parenthesis.
hints.targeted: Check whether the semicolon right after the condition should be removed so the block below belongs to it.

hints.concept: An assignment stores the value on the right into the variable on the left.
hints.guidance: Compare both sides of this assignment and think about what actually changes after it runs.
hints.targeted: Check whether one side of this assignment should be a different variable or expression.

hints.concept: An OR condition is true when at least one side is true.
hints.guidance: Pick a few sample values for the variable and evaluate each side of the OR to see if the whole condition can ever be false.
hints.targeted: Check whether this condition should combine the two checks with && instead of ||.

hints.concept: Strings in Java never change; their methods build and return a brand-new string.
hints.guidance: Think about where the new string produced by this method call actually goes.
hints.targeted: Check whether the result of this call should be assigned back to a variable.

hints.concept: Dividing an integer by zero is not a number Java can produce; it stops the program instead.
hints.guidance: Look at the value on the right side of this division or modulo operation, and ask whether it can ever be 0 when this line runs.
hints.targeted: Check whether the divisor here can be 0 - and what the code should do when it is.

hints.concept: A loop's condition is checked before the first iteration; if it is false, the body never runs.
hints.guidance: Plug the starting value of the counter into the condition and evaluate it by hand.
hints.targeted: Check whether the starting value and the loop bound are the wrong way around.

hints.concept: In an if / else-if chain, only the first branch whose condition is true will run.
hints.guidance: Compare each condition in this chain and think about which branch handles which situation.
hints.targeted: Check whether this repeated condition should test a different value or range.

hints.concept: A while loop only stops when something inside the loop makes its condition false.
hints.guidance: List the variables used in the condition and find the line inside the loop that changes any of them.
hints.targeted: Check whether the loop body should update the variable used in the while condition.

hints.concept: When both numbers in a division are whole numbers, Java does whole-number division and throws the remainder away.
hints.guidance: Look at the types of the two values being divided, not at the type of the variable the answer is stored in.
hints.targeted: Check whether one side of this division should be a decimal value before the division happens.

hints.concept: Most decimal fractions, like 0.1, cannot be stored exactly in a double, so two calculations that should agree can differ by a tiny amount.
hints.guidance: Think about how close two decimal results need to be to count as the same, rather than whether they match exactly.
hints.targeted: Check whether this comparison should allow a small tolerance instead of using == or !=.

hints.concept: x++ increases x, but the value it hands back is the value x had before the increase.
hints.guidance: Follow the order: the old value is read, x goes up by one, and then the assignment stores the old value back.
hints.targeted: Check whether this line should increase the variable without assigning the result back to it.

hints.concept: An AND condition is true only when both of its sides are true at the same time.
hints.guidance: Write down the values that make each side true, and look for a value that appears in both lists.
hints.targeted: Check whether one of the numbers in this condition is wrong, or whether the two checks should be combined with || instead.

hints.concept: A loop over an array should visit every position from the first index to the last one, unless it deliberately needs fewer.
hints.guidance: Work out the value of the counter on the loop's final pass, and compare it with the index of the last element.
hints.targeted: Check whether this loop condition stops one pass too soon, so the element at the end is never processed.

hints.concept: An index such as i + 1 reaches one position further than i, so the loop has to stop early enough for it to stay inside the array.
hints.guidance: On the loop's last pass, write down the value of i and then of i + 1 (or i - 1). Does that position exist?
hints.targeted: Check whether the loop runs far enough that this neighbour index goes past the end (or before the start) of the array.

hints.concept: In nested loops each counter has its own job: the outer one picks the row or the first element, the inner one moves along.
hints.guidance: Trace two passes of the inner loop. Does this index change from one inner pass to the next?
hints.targeted: Check whether this index should use the inner loop's counter rather than the outer one.

hints.concept: A for loop's three parts - start, condition and update - should all be about the same counter.
hints.guidance: Read the loop header aloud: which variable does it start, which does it test, and which does it change?
hints.targeted: Check whether this loop's condition or update uses another loop's counter instead of its own.

hints.concept: A for loop already moves its counter on every pass; changing it again inside the body makes the loop jump.
hints.guidance: Trace the counter through three passes, counting every place it changes. Which elements get visited?
hints.targeted: Check whether this extra change to the counter skips elements you meant to process.

hints.concept: A running total has to be set to its starting value once, before the loop that builds it up.
hints.guidance: Trace the variable through two passes of the loop. What does it hold at the start of the second pass?
hints.targeted: Check whether this line throws away the running value on every pass, so only the last pass counts.

hints.concept: A search for the largest or smallest value needs a starting value that any real value can beat - usually the first element.
hints.guidance: Try the loop on an array where every value is negative (for a maximum) or every value is large (for a minimum).
hints.targeted: Check whether this starting value can win the comparison before any element of the data has been seen.

hints.concept: A return inside a loop ends the whole method at once, so it should only happen once the answer is certain.
hints.guidance: Ask what the method should answer when the first element does not match but a later one does.
hints.targeted: Check whether this part of the loop leaves the method on every pass, so the loop never reaches the second element.

hints.concept: An if / else if chain stops at the first test that is true, so the order of the tests matters.
hints.guidance: Pick a value that should reach the later branch and walk it through the tests from the top.
hints.targeted: Check whether an earlier test already catches every value this branch is meant for, so it can never run.

hints.concept: Without braces, an if or a loop controls exactly one statement; indentation does not change that.
hints.guidance: Which statements run when the condition is false? Mark where the controlled part really ends.
hints.targeted: Check whether the indented line below is meant to be controlled by this if or loop, and add braces if it is.

hints.concept: && and || stop as soon as the left side decides the answer; & and | always evaluate both sides.
hints.guidance: What happens to the right side of this condition when the left side is already false (or already true)?
hints.targeted: Check whether the right side of this condition is only safe when the left side is true, and use && or || if so.
